| INV-PRESENTATION-08 | The mobile a11y floor holds on every diverged or reflowed surface ([[adr-0050]]) — at <768px a household member can read the surface's **primary value without horizontal scroll** and every interactive control is a **≥44px tap target**. First landed on the dashboard (#507), which satisfies the doctrine's "grid → single-column stack" transform by **pure CSS reflow** (no `useIsMobile` renderer split): the header toolbar stacks, the group-breakdown label lifts above its bar+amount, and the second-currency select, `MonthPickerPopover`, `ReportPdfButton`, and rebuild links all size up to the 44px floor on phones. Renderer-independent per ADR-0050 — a truth of whichever layout is active, not of a specific renderer. Extended to the Income screen (#508), the first **bespoke** (non-descriptor) "wide table → stacked cards" renderer split: `IncomeList` picks `IncomeCard` vs `IncomeRowDesktop` at 768px, the amount is promoted to the card headline and the ⋮ action sizes to `size-11`. Extended again to the Tags breakdown (#509): `TagBreakdownSection` picks `TagBreakdownCards` vs `TagBreakdownTable` at 768px, the net value is promoted to the card headline and the pie-inclusion toggle is a `min-h-11` `<label>`; the report/management page order also flips (report first, management card last) as the shared base for the mobile layout. Extended again to the three group hubs (#510, `AssetsHome` / `InvestmentsHome` / `LiabilitiesHome`): already single-column chart stacks (only `InvestmentsHome`'s pie pair is a grid, already `md:grid-cols-2`), so like the dashboard the transform is **pure CSS reflow** — the header toolbar stacks below the title (`flex-col` → `md:flex-row`) and each `size="sm"` bulk-entry button sizes up (`h-11` → `md:h-8`); the shared chart components are unchanged. The same #510 pass also retrofits the floor onto the pre-existing [[adr-0043]] descriptor **list cards** (`PositionListCards`, all ten position types incl. receivables): the split is old (INV-PRESENTATION-05) but predated this floor, so the header action buttons are promoted to primary actions (fill the row, `size-11`) and the shared `RowActionsMenu` ⋮ trigger is prop-driven per renderer — `variant="outline"` + `size-11` on the card (matching `IncomeRowMenu`), bare `ghost` `size-8` in the table — and the shared per-currency headlines (`ListHeadline` + `InvestmentListHeadline`) stack one figure per line on mobile (`block md:inline`, `·` separator `hidden md:inline`) instead of running a mixed-currency total off the primary figure's right edge — single-currency unchanged. Extended again to the two Settings rate tables (#511, `FxRatesCard` / `InflationRatesCard`): each applies the "wide table → stacked cards" transform to its entered-rates list at 768px (the shared add form stays single-layout), the rate promoted to the card headline (`tabular-nums`) and the delete control an icon button at `size-11`; both leaves share the `fx-rate-row` / `inflation-rate-row` testids. Extended again to the ten shared-shell **detail pages** (#535, [[adr-0051]] Phase B): with all ten already on `PositionDetailScreen`, the reflow lands **once** in the core primitives rather than per page — `InfoGrid` reflows its two-column grid to stacked label/value pairs (`md:contents` dissolves the per-pair wrapper back into the grid on desktop), the header stacks (`flex-col` → `md:flex-row`) and its action row wraps, and `HistorySection` picks a stacked card list vs the wide table at 768px (`useIsMobile`) via an optional `renderCard` on the section spec — column-neutral, so a shape not yet carded falls back to the table. The **amount-only** snapshot shape rides it first: the shared `SnapshotCard` (paired with `SnapshotRow` through `useSnapshotRow` + `SnapshotRowMenu`, same `snapshot-row` / `snapshot-amount` testids) promotes the amount to the card headline and sizes the ⋮ to `size-11`, flipping all five amount-only pages (BankAccount / Property / Vehicle / Liability / Receivable); the qty×price / accrued / transaction shapes ride the same scaffold in #536 / #537 / #538. Closed out by a cross-cutting **secondary-control tap-target sweep** (#542): B1 floored only the single promoted primary action per surface, leaving the remaining `size="sm"` controls at ~32px on phones — the detail snapshot-section header (Export / Import / carryover) and actions row (back / Help / Edit / Terminate / Delete), the Income regularity filter, and the Settings Erase / Reactivation / Invite secondary buttons — so each now carries `min-h-11 md:min-h-0` (≥44px below 768px, natural `size-sm` from 768px up); the same pass fixed a B1 gap where the **primary** qty×price / accrued-interest snapshot triggers were themselves left at `size="sm"`, promoting them to the `h-11 md:h-8` primary floor already worn by the amount-only `CreateSnapshotDialog`. #542 also gives both section headers a **deliberate two-row layout** (stacked on phones, inline from 768px): the snapshot header splits **create** (`snapshot-create-row` — Copy carryover + New) from **I/O** (`snapshot-io-row` — Export + Import, `renderImportControl` split out of `renderCreateControls`), with **Copy carryover promoted primary** (solid + `h-11 md:h-8`, since "same as last month" is the common month-close) and New demoted to the secondary outline floor unless it stands alone on the first-ever snapshot; the transactions header (stock / mutualFund / gold / bond) splits **trades** (`txn-trades-row` — Buy primary, Sell, plus Maturity for bond) from **cash flows** (`txn-cashflow-row` — dividend/distribution/coupon income + fees); the same treatment reaches the position **actions row** (Help + Edit above, Close/Status + Delete below). On phones every one of these rows — snapshot, transaction, and actions — goes **full width with its buttons splitting the width evenly** (`max-md:[&>*]:flex-1`), collapsing back to natural inline widths from 768px up (the shared `HistorySection` header wrapper carries `max-md:w-full` so the nested rows can stretch past its `items-start` column). The same treatment reaches the investment-subtype **list filter**: the `RiskProfileFilter` chip bar fills the width and splits its four options evenly on phones (each clearing the 44px floor), and the "show closed positions" toggle drops **below** the chips (`flex-col` → `md:flex-row md:justify-between`) instead of sharing their row. The floor then moves **into the shared primitives** (#559), because every sweep up to and including #542 raised controls one callsite at a time (`min-h-11 md:min-h-0`) while `Button` (`h-8` default / `h-7` sm / `h-9` lg) and `Input` (`h-8`) stayed below the floor by default — so each new screen re-opened the hole and the floor held only where someone remembered to type the class: the three **text** button sizes and `Input` now carry `max-md:min-h-11` in the variant itself, and #542's per-callsite sprinkles are removed as redundant in the same pass. `icon*` is deliberately excluded (square — a bare `min-h-11` renders it 44×32; the mobile-visible icon buttons stay hand-floored to `size-11` per #510/#511/#535, the rest are absolutely-positioned dialog/sheet/sidebar close affordances), `xs`/`icon-xs` stay dense on purpose, and a callsite that genuinely needs a denser control opts out with `max-md:min-h-0` (tailwind-merge lets the callsite win). The same pass closes **Settings**, the surface #542 named but never reached — the verification found ~25 controls between 20px and 36px there, and the reason none of them tripped the gate is that no `settings-mobile.spec.ts` existed and no Settings component had a unit test, so `qa-strict` stayed green on *other* surfaces' coverage. What the primitives cannot reach is hand-floored: the three `SettingsScreen` `<select>`s (at the time there was **no `ui/select.tsx`** — all 34 `<select>` callsites hand-rolled `h-9`, 28 of them dialogs, so a shared select primitive was deferred to #541, which added it), the checkbox/radio hit rows in `SettingsScreen` / `BackupPanel` / `RestorePanel`, and the three Settings text links. Verified in `dashboard-mobile.spec.ts`, `income-mobile.spec.ts`, `tags-mobile.spec.ts`, `hubs-mobile.spec.ts`, `list-mobile.spec.ts`, `settings-rates-mobile.spec.ts`, `settings-mobile.spec.ts` (which also pins the ≥768px density, so "raise everything to 44px" can't silently pad the desktop forms) and `detail-mobile.spec.ts` / `detail-mobile-qtyprice.spec.ts` / `detail-mobile-accrued.spec.ts` / `detail-mobile-transactions.spec.ts` (@smoke, 390px) + `IncomeList.test.tsx` / `TagBreakdownSection.test.tsx` / `FxRatesCard.test.tsx` / `InflationRatesCard.test.tsx` / `HistorySection.test.tsx` / `detail-mobile.test.tsx` / `detail-mobile-qtyprice.test.tsx` / `detail-mobile-accrued.test.tsx` / `detail-mobile-transactions.test.tsx` / `RiskProfileFilter.test.tsx` (renderer conformance) + `tapFloor.test.tsx` (the primitive floor contract — jsdom has no layout, so it pins the class, and the @smoke specs pin the pixels). The last surface the floor had not reached is the **create/edit dialog form bodies** (#541) — deliberately held out of the #428 B-series and out of [[adr-0051]], since they are the opaque `renderEditDialog`. A 390px pass scoped what actually breached the bar, and most of the suspected breaks did **not**: the forms fit a 390x844 viewport with the footer reachable, and the unconditional two-column rows render a `type="date"` field and its picker icon in full at ~157px — so per the doctrine's "merely cramped stays single-layout" they were left alone rather than stacked. Three things did breach. First, **`<select>` had no primitive to floor**: all 34 callsites hand-rolled `h-9 rounded-md border border-input bg-background px-3 text-sm` at 36px, so unlike `Button`/`Input` after #559 every new form re-opened the hole — `ui/select.tsx` now carries the same `max-md:min-h-11` contract (plus `text-base md:text-sm`, which is load bearing rather than cosmetic: iOS Safari zooms the viewport when a control under 16px takes focus, which the old `text-sm` selects did on every tap), and all 34 callsites are migrated. Second, the **ownership radios** had no hit row: the native ~13px dot sat in a `flex items-center gap-2` label about 20px tall. The `<label>` already wrapped its input so tapping the word worked — what was missing was a target to aim at — and because all 22 position Create/Edit dialogs had hand-inlined the same block it could not be fixed in one place, so it is extracted to a shared `OwnershipField` (both options now in `max-md:min-h-11` rows splitting the full width on phones, natural inline width from 768px). The extraction also collapses ~950 duplicated lines, standardises on `common:` (the `investments:ownership.*` keys were byte-identical duplicates in both locales and are deleted), and scopes the radio-group `name` per dialog — eight of them shared a bare `ownership_type`, which would have let two mounted dialogs steal each other's selection. Third, the one **`grid-cols-3`** row (liability term / start / maturity) leaves ~100px per column at 390px and truncated the year off both date fields, so it alone stacks below 768px. Two non-breaching cleanups ride along: `max-h-[90vh] overflow-y-auto` moves into `DialogContent` (twelve tall dialogs passed exactly those classes by hand and 31 did not — purely defensive, since nothing observably clipped, but a `fixed` translate-centred shell has no other way to reach a footer once content outgrows the viewport), and the two-column rows get `[&>*]:content-end` so a wrapped label in one column no longer desynchronises the inputs' baselines. Verified in `dialogs-mobile.spec.ts` (@smoke, 390px — which also pins the ≥768px density, so the floor cannot silently pad the desktop forms) + `OwnershipField.test.tsx` and the `Select` block of `tapFloor.test.tsx`. | `frontend/e2e/dashboard-mobile.spec.ts`<br>`frontend/e2e/detail-mobile-accrued.spec.ts`<br>`frontend/e2e/detail-mobile-qtyprice.spec.ts`<br>`frontend/e2e/detail-mobile-transactions.spec.ts`<br>`frontend/e2e/detail-mobile.spec.ts`<br>`frontend/e2e/dialogs-mobile.spec.ts`<br>`frontend/e2e/hubs-mobile.spec.ts`<br>`frontend/e2e/income-mobile.spec.ts`<br>`frontend/e2e/list-mobile.spec.ts`<br>`frontend/e2e/settings-mobile.spec.ts`<br>`frontend/e2e/settings-rates-mobile.spec.ts`<br>`frontend/e2e/tags-mobile.spec.ts`<br>`frontend/src/components/common/FxRatesCard.test.tsx`<br>`frontend/src/components/common/InflationRatesCard.test.tsx`<br>`frontend/src/components/common/OwnershipField.test.tsx`<br>`frontend/src/components/common/RiskProfileFilter.test.tsx`<br>`frontend/src/components/detail/detail-mobile-accrued.test.tsx`<br>`frontend/src/components/detail/detail-mobile-qtyprice.test.tsx`<br>`frontend/src/components/detail/detail-mobile-transactions.test.tsx`<br>`frontend/src/components/detail/detail-mobile.test.tsx`<br>`frontend/src/components/income/IncomeList.test.tsx`<br>`frontend/src/components/screens/SettingsScreen.test.tsx`<br>`frontend/src/components/tags/TagBreakdownSection.test.tsx`<br>`frontend/src/components/ui/tapFloor.test.tsx` |
| INV-PRESENTATION-06 | The shared Position Create/Edit dialog scaffold (`PositionFormDialog`, ADR-0043 follow-on / #334) owns the plumbing every per-type dialog duplicated: the dialog shell + header, the `<form>` wrapper, the **shared error envelope** (`errorMessage`, the ADR-0027 face), and the footer (cancel + submit with a distinct pending label + disabled-in-flight). It exposes two modes — **create** (self-triggering, owns its own open state, resets via `onClosed` on close) and **edit** (controlled via `open`/`onOpenChange`, no trigger) — and hands the caller a `close` callback through `onSubmit(close)` so the type keeps its own payload mapping and submit guards while the scaffold owns dismissal. The field **body stays hand-written** per type (no field-config DSL); the dirty-guard is deliberately out of scope. Verified in `PositionFormDialog.test.tsx` (synthetic body — asserts the shell contract, not one type's fields) | `frontend/src/components/dialogs/PositionFormDialog.test.tsx` |
| INV-PRESENTATION-09 | The app paints in its **bundled** typeface, not the platform's — the first family the app tree resolves is `"Geist Variable"` (from `@fontsource-variable/geist`, shipped in the bundle), with the system stack demoted to a fallback tail that applies only if the webfont fails. The rule lives in exactly one place (`--font-sans`, reaching the tree through the `html { @apply font-sans }` base layer); a competing `font-family` on `body` or any wrapper above the app silently beats it by inheritance, which is how the app spent its pre-#565 life downloading a woff2 on every cold load and then rendering in `system-ui`. Not a cosmetic row: `system-ui` resolves to a **different physical font per platform**, so while the override held, every text-width assertion in the suite was platform-dependent — the #562 settings carry-over copy measured 268.6px locally and 301px on the Linux CI runner for the same string (~12%), which is what makes width-sensitive copy assertions reproducible now that it's fixed. It is also the screen half of a two-sided contract: the PDF report renderer embeds the same Geist (`backend/internal/reports/pdf/render.go`), so an exported report and the screen it came from are one typeface. E2E-native rather than vitest because jsdom has no font stack and does not resolve `@apply`, so the regression is invisible to a unit test; the check pairs the computed first family with a canvas measurement against the generic fallback, since `document.fonts.check()` returns `true` both when a face is loaded and when no matching `@font-face` exists at all (it reported `true` throughout the bug). Verified in `typography.spec.ts` (@smoke) | `frontend/e2e/typography.spec.ts` |
